title: Strong Nouns — Feminine ō-Stems
subtitle: Giefu, lufu, lār — the feminine parallel to masculine a-stems.
objectives: Understand and apply the concepts of Strong Nouns — Feminine ō-Stems.
Read and parse examples from authentic Old English texts.

sections.heading: Core concept
sections.body: Feminine ō-stems end in -u or a vowel in the nominative singular. The genitive and dative singular both end in -e. The nominative plural ends in -a or -e.

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: Giefu (gift): sēo giefu (nom), þā giefe (acc), þǣre giefe (gen/dat). Plural: þā giefa.

items.prompt: What is the main concept of this lesson?

items.answer: Review the paradigm and example above.
